meta.name: Microsoft Cybersecurity Architect Expert (SC-100)
meta.notes: Initial pack: 10 questions covering Zero Trust strategy, SOC and identity architecture, regulatory compliance design, infrastructure security posture, and application and data security strategy across Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, and multicloud environments. | 2026-05-23 keyword-balance pass | 2026-06-01 +6 questions to unlock learning path

questions.question: An organization adopting Zero Trust must enforce explicit verification on every workload request, regardless of the source network. Which architectural pattern most directly implements the verify-explicitly pillar across Microsoft Entra workloads?
options: Place all corporate workloads behind a single perimeter VPN that authenticates users once — VPN-based perimeter access does not evaluate per-request Microsoft Entra signals such as user risk, device compliance, or workload sensitivity
Require Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies that evaluate user, device compliance, location, application, and real-time risk signals on every sign-in to every workload
Issue long-lived service principal secrets to all application identities and rotate the secrets every 90 days through an automated Azure Key Vault rotation policy schedule
Apply a single Entra security defaults baseline tenant-wide that enforces MFA only on administrative accounts and leaves standard user sign-ins unchallenged on the tenant
questions.explanation: Verify-explicitly requires authenticating and authorizing every request using all available signals — identity, device posture, location, application, and real-time risk. Entra Conditional Access is the policy engine that evaluates those signals at every sign-in. A perimeter VPN implicitly trusts whatever sits behind it, which is the opposite of Zero Trust. Long-lived secrets rotated periodically still embed implicit trust between rotations. Security defaults are a minimal baseline that does not implement per-request signal-driven authorization.
questions.domain: Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities

questions.question: A CISO wants to consolidate three legacy SIEM products and reduce mean time to respond across endpoint, identity, email, and cloud telemetry. Which Microsoft pattern best satisfies a converged SOC strategy?
options: Use Microsoft Sentinel as the only destination with Defender XDR's automatic incident creation and email alerting — routing all Defender XDR incidents to Sentinel alone duplicates triage work and loses the unified cross-product email signal correlation that XDR provides natively
Use Microsoft Defender XDR only, since the unified Defender portal handles incidents, hunting, and automation across products and makes a SIEM unnecessary going forward
Retain each existing SIEM, forward Defender XDR alerts to all three via the Microsoft Graph Security API, and rely on a custom correlation layer built by the security team
Use Microsoft Defender XDR for native correlation across endpoints, identities, email, and apps, and use Microsoft Sentinel as the SIEM for remaining log sources and case management
questions.explanation: Microsoft's reference SOC architecture pairs Defender XDR (native cross-product correlation for endpoints, identities, email, apps) with Sentinel as the SIEM/SOAR for additional log sources, long-term retention, and case management. Disabling XDR's incident creation breaks native correlation. Defender XDR alone cannot ingest arbitrary non-Microsoft telemetry. Retaining three SIEMs in parallel keeps the silos the consolidation was meant to remove.
questions.domain: Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities

questions.question: External partners must access a curated set of internal applications using credentials from their existing Microsoft Entra tenants, without you provisioning shadow accounts. Which design satisfies the requirement with the least overhead?
options: Configure Microsoft Entra cross-tenant access settings and B2B collaboration so partner identities are invited as guests and governed through entitlement management access packages

Stand up an Active Directory Federation Services farm in the perimeter to federate partner identity — ADFS provides legacy federation but requires the partner's domain and identity to be explicitly configured, rather than using Entra cross-tenant access for per-partner attribute-based policies
Synchronize each partner directory into your tenant with Microsoft Entra Connect cloud sync so partner users appear as fully provisioned member accounts inside your own tenant directory
Issue every partner an internal Microsoft Entra member account, enforce MFA on it, and rotate the credential every 30 days through a documented manual process owned by the help desk
questions.explanation: Cross-tenant access settings plus B2B collaboration let partner identities authenticate against their own home tenant while you authorize them as guests, with entitlement management automating access reviews and lifecycle. ADFS still issues local AD accounts and creates significant operational burden. Connect cloud sync of a partner directory turns external users into member identities you must govern. Issuing internal accounts and rotating credentials is exactly the shadow-account model the requirement forbids.

questions.question: An organization in scope of PCI DSS and HIPAA needs a single view of control coverage across Azure and AWS that maps each control to both frameworks. Which Microsoft service should anchor the design?
options: Microsoft Sentinel content hub solutions for PCI DSS and HIPAA, deployed against a workspace that ingests AWS CloudTrail events through the Amazon Web Services data connector
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager assessments with the PCI DSS and HIPAA templates, scored against the in-scope Microsoft 365 tenant rather than the AWS account workloads
Microsoft Defender for Cloud regulatory compliance dashboard with the PCI DSS and HIPAA/HITRUST standards added to the AWS connector and the Azure subscriptions in scope
Azure Policy regulatory compliance built-in initiative assignments at Azure management groups, replicated as service control policies inside the AWS organization through scripting
questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud's regulatory compliance dashboard evaluates Azure and AWS resources against PCI DSS, HIPAA/HITRUST, ISO 27001, NIST and other standards through a single pane. Sentinel solutions deliver detections and workbooks, not control-coverage scoring. Purview Compliance Manager scores Microsoft 365/Azure controls only, not AWS workloads. Azure Policy applies to Azure resources; replicating it as AWS SCPs through scripting is brittle and does not produce framework-mapped scoring.

questions.question: A new Azure landing zone must continuously evaluate posture against the Microsoft cloud security benchmark and apply preventive guardrails at the management-group scope. Which combination achieves this with the least drift?
options: Enable Defender for Cloud on each individual subscription and assign MCSB per subscription without a root management group scope — per-subscription enablement misses new subscriptions added later and cannot enforce the policy at the root management group scope
Enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud at the root management group with MCSB assigned as the default standard and Azure Policy initiatives deployed at management-group scope as guardrails
Use Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules to detect deviations from MCSB and trigger Logic Apps playbooks that remediate drift after the fact at the resource level inside each subscription
Use Azure Blueprints assigned at every subscription to package MCSB and policy guardrails together, accepting that blueprints are now deprecated but still functional during the transition
questions.explanation: Enabling Defender for Cloud at the root management group inherits MCSB to every subscription beneath it, and Azure Policy initiatives at management-group scope apply preventive guardrails (deny/audit/deployIfNotExists) without per-subscription drift. Per-subscription enablement and ARM templates require continuous reconciliation. Sentinel + playbooks react after a deviation has already happened, not preventatively. Blueprints are deprecated and Microsoft's published guidance is to move to policy at management-group scope instead.

questions.question: Hybrid Windows and Linux servers spread across Azure, AWS, and on-premises must receive EDR, vulnerability assessment, and file integrity monitoring through one control plane. Which design meets the requirement?
options: Onboard non-Azure servers through Azure Arc, then enable Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2 on the connected subscriptions to deliver EDR, vulnerability assessment, and FIM uniformly

Install Microsoft Defender for Endpoint directly on every server without Azure Arc — Defender for Endpoint provides EDR telemetry but does not surface the server's configuration through Azure Arc or provide Azure cloud security posture assessment for the non-Azure server
Forward Windows event logs and Linux syslog to Microsoft Sentinel and build custom KQL analytics to approximate EDR detections, vulnerability findings, and file integrity changes per host
Deploy the Microsoft Monitoring Agent on every server reporting into a Log Analytics workspace and rely on Update Management plus Change Tracking to substitute for EDR and FIM coverage
questions.explanation: Azure Arc projects non-Azure servers into Azure Resource Manager so that subscription-scoped Defender for Servers Plan 2 can deliver Defender for Endpoint EDR, integrated vulnerability assessment, and file integrity monitoring under one control plane. MDE alone gives EDR but leaves vulnerability assessment and FIM as separate point products. Sentinel KQL approximations are detective, not preventive, and miss kernel-level EDR. MMA + Update Management + Change Tracking covers neither EDR nor file integrity monitoring.

questions.question: A hub-and-spoke topology must inspect all spoke-to-spoke traffic and all outbound internet traffic, including TLS inspection on egress. Which strategy delivers this with the least operational burden?
options: Deploy a network security group on every spoke subnet with explicit deny rules for cross-spoke traffic — NSGs operate at L3/L4 and cannot perform deep-packet inspection or TLS decryption for spoke-to-spoke traffic as Azure Firewall Premium does
Deploy Azure Application Gateway with Web Application Firewall in the hub and route all spoke-to-spoke and outbound internet traffic through the Application Gateway listeners and backend pools
Deploy Azure Firewall Premium in the hub virtual network, force spoke-to-spoke and outbound traffic through it via user-defined routes, and enable TLS inspection on Azure Firewall Premium
Peer every spoke virtual network directly to every other spoke in a full mesh and apply NSG rules at the subnet level to enforce east-west segmentation between application workloads
questions.explanation: Azure Firewall Premium in the hub, combined with UDRs that send spoke and outbound traffic to it, performs stateful inspection and adds TLS inspection and IDPS without per-spoke configuration. NSGs filter at layer 4 only and cannot perform TLS inspection. Application Gateway is a reverse proxy for HTTP(S) inbound web workloads, not a general-purpose egress/inter-VNet inspection device. A full spoke-to-spoke mesh sidesteps central inspection and scales as O(n^2) peerings.

questions.question: A CISO needs visibility into shadow IT use, session controls on sanctioned SaaS applications, and data loss prevention on third-party cloud storage. Which design anchors the SaaS security strategy?
options: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Safe Links and Safe Attachments scoped to all Exchange mailboxes — Defender for Office 365 protects email and Office 365 apps in the cloud but does not discover or control shadow SaaS apps accessed via browser or provide cloud session-level inline policies

Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention policies scoped to Microsoft 365 workloads only — Purview DLP does not discover unsanctioned cloud storage providers or apply inline session control policies to third-party SaaS apps accessed via browser
Microsoft Sentinel data connectors for each individual SaaS vendor, with analytics rules that detect anomalous activity and Logic Apps playbooks that revoke user sessions after every detection
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps with cloud discovery from firewall logs, Conditional Access app control for session policies, and file policies on connected third-party SaaS storage providers
questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud Apps is the SaaS-security control plane: cloud discovery surfaces shadow IT from firewall/proxy logs, Conditional Access app control routes sessions through a reverse proxy to enforce session policies, and connected app file policies apply DLP across third-party cloud storage. Defender for Office 365 protects mail; it does not deliver SaaS session control. Purview M365 DLP does not cover third-party SaaS. Sentinel ingests SaaS logs for detection but does not enforce inline session controls.

questions.question: Developers must scan repositories for secrets and vulnerable dependencies, block merges on findings, and surface results to the SOC. Which Microsoft-aligned combination satisfies the requirement?
options: GitHub Advanced Security with secret scanning, Dependabot, and CodeQL, branch protection rules that require checks to pass, and an integration that forwards alerts into Microsoft Sentinel
Azure Pipelines that invoke a third-party SAST tool nightly, with results emailed to the developer who last committed and a manual SOC ticket opened when the scanner reports any finding
Microsoft Defender for Cloud DevOps security alerts only, with no branch protection enforced in the repository and no required status checks gating merges into the protected main branch
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps file policies applied to the GitHub organization's repositories to detect committed secrets after they have been merged into the protected main branch
questions.explanation: GitHub Advanced Security provides secret scanning, Dependabot dependency review, and CodeQL static analysis. Branch protection requiring those checks to pass blocks merges on findings, and a connector forwards alerts into Sentinel for SOC triage. Nightly third-party scanning is detective and post-merge, not preventive. Defender for Cloud DevOps surfaces findings but cannot enforce branch protection on its own. Defender for Cloud Apps file policies operate on SaaS storage data planes, not on Git pull-request gating.
questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data

questions.question: Sensitive financial documents must be auto-classified, encrypted at rest and in transit, and prevented from leaving the tenant by email or external sharing. Which combination defines the data security architecture?
options: BitLocker on every endpoint that stores documents locally, TLS enforced on inbound HTTPS, and an Exchange transport rule that blocks any external recipient address on outbound mail flows
Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels with auto-labeling that applies encryption rights, Microsoft Purview DLP policies for Exchange and SharePoint, and label-aware sharing restrictions in Teams
Customer-managed keys in Azure Key Vault for all storage accounts holding documents, no classification labels, and reliance on Conditional Access to block external sharing entirely tenant-wide

Azure Information Protection unified labeling client on every endpoint with manual classification — manual labeling relies on user action and does not provide the auto-labeling that automatically applies sensitivity labels and encryption without user intervention
questions.explanation: Purview sensitivity labels with auto-labeling classify content based on trainable classifiers, sensitive info types, or keywords and apply Rights Management encryption that persists with the file. Purview DLP for Exchange and SharePoint blocks risky transmission, and label-aware Teams/SharePoint sharing controls restrict guest access on labeled content. BitLocker plus a blanket external-block transport rule is blunt and lacks classification. CMKs only re-key storage; they do not classify or prevent egress. The AIP unified labeling client has been retired in favor of built-in Microsoft 365 Apps labeling, and manual-only classification with no DLP misses the requirement.
questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data

questions.question: An architect is designing privileged access for Azure subscriptions under Zero Trust. Administrators must hold no standing high-privilege roles; instead, elevated access should be requested just in time, time-bound, and require approval and MFA. Which Microsoft capability should anchor this design?
options: Assign administrators permanent Owner roles but require a Conditional Access policy enforcing MFA at every sign-in to those accounts
Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management with eligible role assignments that require activation with approval, MFA, and a time limit
Place all administrators in a single security group and grant it the Owner role at the management-group scope for simplicity
Issue each administrator a separate break-glass account with a standing Global Administrator role stored in a password vault
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM) makes roles eligible rather than permanent, so administrators activate access just in time with approval, MFA, and an expiry — eliminating standing privilege per Zero Trust. Permanent Owner roles with MFA still leave standing high privilege available at all times. A single group holding permanent Owner is even broader standing access. Break-glass accounts are emergency-only and should be tightly controlled exceptions, not the model for routine administration.

questions.question: An organization wants threat intelligence and detection rules to be evaluated against the MITRE ATT&CK framework so the SOC can identify coverage gaps across tactics and techniques. Which design best provides ATT&CK-aligned coverage visibility within the Microsoft stack?
options: Export all Microsoft Sentinel logs to a third-party spreadsheet and manually tag each analytics rule with an ATT&CK technique ID once per quarter
Rely on Microsoft Defender XDR alert titles alone, mapping each to a tactic by reading the alert description during incident triage
Use the Microsoft Sentinel MITRE ATT&CK coverage view to map active analytics rules and hunting queries to tactics and techniques and reveal gaps
Assign an Azure Policy initiative that audits whether each subscription has any analytics rule enabled, regardless of which technique it detects
questions.explanation: Microsoft Sentinel includes a MITRE ATT&CK coverage view that maps active analytics rules and hunting queries onto the ATT&CK matrix, directly revealing which tactics and techniques are covered or have gaps. Manually tagging rules in a spreadsheet is error-prone and not maintained continuously. Reading Defender XDR alert titles during triage gives no systematic framework-wide coverage picture. An Azure Policy audit of whether any rule exists says nothing about which techniques are covered.

questions.question: A Zero Trust network strategy for Azure PaaS data services must ensure that traffic from application subnets to Azure Storage and Azure SQL never traverses the public internet and that the services are not reachable from public endpoints. Which design satisfies both goals?
options: Enable service endpoints on the application subnets and keep the storage and SQL public endpoints enabled for compatibility
Deploy Azure Private Endpoints for the storage and SQL resources and disable their public network access so they are reachable only privately
Restrict the storage and SQL resource firewalls to the application subnet's public outbound IP address ranges only
Route all outbound application traffic through an Azure NAT gateway so the source IP is stable and allow-listed on each service
questions.explanation: Private Endpoints give the PaaS services private IPs inside the VNet so traffic stays on the Microsoft backbone, and disabling public network access removes the public endpoint entirely — satisfying both requirements. Service endpoints keep the public endpoint reachable and route over Azure's network but do not give a private IP or remove public exposure. Firewalling to outbound public IPs still uses the public endpoint and exposes it to allow-listed addresses. A NAT gateway only stabilizes the source IP; the services remain publicly reachable.

questions.question: An architect must design API security so that a customer-facing API published through Azure API Management is protected from the OWASP Top 10 and from volumetric DDoS, while API Management still enforces token validation. Which layered design is most appropriate?
options: Rely solely on API Management rate-limit policies to absorb volumetric attacks and to block injection and cross-site scripting payloads
Place Azure Front Door with WAF in front of API Management for OWASP protection and DDoS Protection at the network edge, with API Management validating JWTs
Expose API Management directly to the internet and enable Microsoft Defender for APIs as the only inspection layer for both DDoS and OWASP threats
Put an internal load balancer in front of API Management and use network security groups to block known malicious source IP ranges
questions.explanation: Layering Azure Front Door with WAF in front of API Management addresses OWASP Top 10 attacks at the edge, Azure DDoS Protection mitigates volumetric attacks, and API Management still validates JWTs — a defense-in-depth design. API Management rate limits throttle volume but do not provide WAF rule inspection for injection or XSS. Defender for APIs adds detection and posture insight but is not a WAF or DDoS mitigation control. An internal load balancer with NSG IP blocking is L3/L4 only and cannot inspect application-layer OWASP payloads.
questions.domain: Design security solutions for applications and data

questions.question: A board mandates a quantified, prioritized roadmap to improve the organization's security posture across Microsoft 365 identity, devices, and apps, expressed as a single trackable score with recommended actions. Which Microsoft capability should the architect use to frame this roadmap?
options: Microsoft Secure Score, which quantifies posture across identity, devices, and apps and recommends prioritized improvement actions
Microsoft Sentinel workbooks that visualize incident volumes over time as a proxy for the organization's overall posture
The Microsoft Defender for Cloud secure score, which scores only Azure resource configuration and excludes Microsoft 365 identity and apps
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, which scores regulatory control implementation rather than operational security posture
questions.explanation: Microsoft Secure Score gives a single quantified measure of Microsoft 365 security posture across identity, devices, and apps with prioritized improvement actions, ideal for a board-level roadmap. Sentinel workbooks visualize incident telemetry, not a posture score with recommended actions. The Defender for Cloud secure score scopes to Azure (and multicloud) resource configuration, not Microsoft 365 identity and apps. Compliance Manager scores progress against regulatory controls, which is compliance rather than operational security posture.

questions.question: Threat modeling for a payment microservice running on Azure Kubernetes Service must ensure that a compromised pod cannot reach secrets or other namespaces, and that container images are verified before deployment. Which combination best reflects a Zero Trust workload design?
options: Grant the AKS cluster a single highly privileged service account shared by all pods and store secrets in Kubernetes generic secrets
Use Kubernetes network policies and per-workload managed identities with Microsoft Defender for Containers and image scanning that gates deployment of unverified images
Disable network policies to simplify pod communication and rely on a perimeter Azure Firewall to block all lateral movement inside the cluster
Run all workloads in the default namespace with a permissive pod security context so the platform team has a single place to apply controls
questions.explanation: Kubernetes network policies segment pod-to-pod and namespace traffic, per-workload managed identities give each pod least-privilege access, and Defender for Containers with image scanning blocks unverified images before deployment — a layered Zero Trust workload design. A single privileged shared service account and generic secrets maximize blast radius. Disabling network policies removes in-cluster segmentation; a perimeter firewall cannot stop east-west movement between pods. Running everything in the default namespace with permissive security contexts removes isolation rather than enforcing it.
